subject: Rack mapping + local persistent cache encryption & pod-affinity plan
messages:
From: Alex Sanders <alex.sanders@heliomed.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem intake: rack mapping and local cache questions

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the prep call last week. Per the intake workshop the ops team flagged two constraints that will affect cluster layout and storage:

- Our datacenter requires encrypted at-rest for removable NVMe (we currently use node-local NVMe for model shard caches).
- The facility network segment limits east-west BGP peering to a single pair and disallows multicast.

We want to finalize the node pool and storage mapping before procurement. Can you confirm whether Redwood's preflight expects local NVMe as a formal cache tier (and how encryption/KMS should be handled), and any recommended pod-affinity rules to keep inference pods on nodes with warmed local caches?

I've attached the rack inventory and FIO logs.

Thanks,
Alex
Ops Lead, HelioMed
attachments: rack-bom-helio.csv, fio-bench-20270620.log

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sanders <alex.sanders@heliomed.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem intake: rack mapping and local cache questions

Alex — thanks, got the attachments. Quick answers up-front, then a proposed follow-up deliverable (MAP).

Short answers:
- Yes: we recommend keeping a node-local NVMe tier for KV/prefix caches and per-model shard hot stores. That reduces load on the networked blockstore and lowers tail latency.
- Encryption: Redwood supports integrating with customer KMS (KMIP or cloud KMS over TLS). For removable NVMe we recommend LUKS with a node-level keywrap managed by your HSM or vault during boot — we can provide init-container tooling that unlocks and mounts LUKS volumes in the kubelet boot sequence.
- Pod affinity: Use a combination of nodeSelector/nodeAffinity + a lightweight admission webhook that prefers nodes with a warmed cache label (e.g., redwood/cache-ready=true). We include a small daemon that reports cache-warmth and exposes a node label via the API.

Proposed deliverable: Redwood-MAP-HelioMed-v1.pdf — canonical action items including: rack-to-node mapping, BIOS/network knobs, KMS integration steps, and a short preflight checklist. Will circulate v1 after we align on the following decisions below.

Primary decisions we need from HelioMed ops:
1) Accept LUKS-on-NVMe with HSM wrapped keys, or insist on hardware native encryption?
2) Can we run a lightweight management agent in a privileged DaemonSet for cache reporting and LUKS unlock?
3) Preferred service egress path for model fetches (BGP pair A vs B) so we can tune cache prefetch to the expected egress path.

I'll schedule a 30m follow-up for Thursday to lock these down.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood-MAP-HelioMed-v1.pdf

From: Alex Sanders <alex.sanders@heliomed.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem intake: rack mapping and local cache questions

Avery — quick replies inline:

1) Hardware encryption is preferred but the vendor's NVMe modules only support controller-bound keys we cannot manage centrally. We can accept LUKS with HSM-wrapped keys as long as key rotation policies are supported.
2) Agent: yes, acceptable for the onboarding window; the team will validate code. Must be auditable and run with least privilege.
3) Egress: Primary egress path is BGP pair Alpha (ASN 64512) — we can provide the BGP neighbor configs during the session.

I'll join the Thursday slot. Also, can you add a draft of pod affinity rules to the MAP so our infra team can pre-review?

Regards,
Alex

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem intake: rack mapping and local cache questions

Thanks Alex + Avery — attaching a short draft of the affinity and cache-handling snippets we intend to include in the MAP. Key points:

- Node pools: control-plane (3x masters, dedicated), infra (logging/metrics, small SSDs), compute-cpu (general inference), compute-nvme (large NVMe 8x1.6TB, local cache), compute-gpu (A100/T4 depending on SKU).
- Storage mapping:
  * Local NVMe: used for per-node model KV cache and transient shard files. Mounted via LUKS; unlock handled by a privileged init DaemonSet that fetches a wrapped key from the HSM and performs cryptsetup.
  * Network blockstore: Rook/Ceph with encrypted OSD disks for weights and long-term artifacts (replication 3, fast tier on SSDs).
  * Backup: nightly snapshot to the customer's S3-compatible object store with server-side encryption.
- Pod affinity rules (draft):
  * requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: nodeAffinity for node.kubernetes.io/role=compute-nvme for pods that need low-latency local cache.
  * preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: label selector redwood/cache-ready=true (weight: 100).
  * anti-affinity to spread replicas across BMC power domains and racks when >1 replica.
- Preflight checks we will run:
  * fio 4k/64k random r/w baseline, kernel tcp_retries2, net.core.rmem_max/tcp_rmem tuning, MTU 9000 checks, bond+LACP validation, BIOS power/perf settings (c-states disabled for GPUs), SR-IOV where requested.

I'll include the actual YAML snippets in MAP v1.

Irene Choi
Infrastructure Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood-MAP-HelioMed-v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Sanders <alex.sanders@heliomed.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem intake: rack mapping and local cache questions

Alex — thanks for the clarifications on keys and egress. Per our internal alignment we added two small items to the MAP and checklist before we finalize procurement:

1) Warmup strategy: a small rolling prefetch job (cronJob) that pulls hot model shards to local NVMe after node maintenance. We will include an opt-in configuration and a size threshold per model.
2) Observability hooks: expose a Prometheus metric redwood_cache_hits_total and a per-node gauge redwood_cache_ready (0/1) so your SREs can alarm on under-warmed nodes.

Next steps:
- We will send MAP v1 (attached) with YAML snippets and the draft DaemonSet for the LUKS-unlock tool.
- Please confirm acceptance of the LUKS approach and whether your HSM supports PKCS#11 or KMIP; we'll adapt the keywrap accordingly.

If all good we'll book a short procurement alignment (15m) next week to attach BOM labels.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions PM, Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood-MAP-HelioMed-v1.pdf, rack-bom-helio.csv
